messages.subject: Clarification of output from annotateWithGeneParts and FeatureFlank
messages.subject_clean: Clarification of output from annotateWithGeneParts and FeatureFlank
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Altuna,

Good day to you. After I run below command:

library(genomation) ;
gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("all_refseq.rn6.bed.txt") ;
diffAnn.all=annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p.all,"GRanges"),gene.obj) ;
dput(diffAnn.all,"a_diffAnn_all.txt") ;
cpg.obj=readFeatureFlank("cpgi.rn6.bed.txt", feature.flank.name <http://feature.flank.name>=c("CpGi", "shores")) ;
diffCpGann.all=annotateWithFeatureFlank(as(myDiff25p.all,"GRanges"), cpg.obj$CpGi,cpg.obj$shores, feature.name <http://feature.name>="CpGi",flank.name <http://flank.name>="shores") ;
dput(diffCpGann.all,"b_diffCpGann_all.txt")

I combined both dput txt.files in table shown something like this:

"a_diffAnn_all.txt" + b_diffCpGann_all.txt
"row.names" "target.row" "dist.to.feature" "feature.name <http://feature.name>" "feature.strand" "prom" "exon" "intron" "CpGi" "shores"
"1" "2400" 1 -21903 "XR_589869.1" 1 0 1 1 0 0
"2" "643" 2 0 "XM_006227857.3" 2 1 1 0 0 0
"3" "3122" 3 0 "NM_138870.1" 1 1 1 1 0 1
"4" "3221" 4 15762 "XM_017589939.1" 2 0 0 0 0 0
"5" "3229" 5 -2047 "XM_017590426.1" 2 0 0 0 0 0
"21" "821" 21 2167 "XM_017590863.1" 2 0 1 1 1 1

Question#1
As for gene type (prom, exon, intron),
"1" overlap in both exon and intron;
"2" overlap in promoter and exon,
"3" overlap in promoter, exon and intron
May I know why certain feature has more than one gene type?

Question#2
"4" - with no overlap in prom, exon and intron, I assume it is in intergenic, right?

Question#3
As for CpG type (CpGi, shores),
"1" with no overlap, i assume it is in others than CpGi and shores, right?

Question#4
"21" overlap in both CpGi and shores,May I know why this feature has more than one CpG type?

Question#5
I would like to clarify what is the target.row means?

Appreciate your clarification again, thanks many.

Best wishes,
Wai Feng

messages.subject: some problems about PCA methyKit package
messages.subject_clean: some problems about PCA methyKit package
messages.body_plain:
Dear Altuna,
        I recently used the methyKit package to analysis methylation data. I encountered some problems about Principal Component Anaysis. Fig A is the result using the methyKit package,  Fig B is the cluster result using the prcomp package.

         Two picture shows the two cluster results are different.  I have some problem about the results. 1) The value of  x  axis and y axis in the two picture are different. In the Fig B , x axis and y axis were  the PC1  and PC2 value respectively ,which were not scaled.  But the value of x axis and y axis  in the Fig A are greater than that in Fig B. Do you do some normalization? How to do it? 2) In the Fig A , we can identify the different cluster clearly, and not in Fig B.  MethyKit and I use the prcomp pakage, why are the cluster results different?
     Look forward to your reply. Thank you very much!

    Best wishes,
    Yanling

we...@big.ac.cn

messages.body_plain:
non-CpG contexts seem more methylated than I would expect, in mammalians non-CpG methylation is rare, I don't know which species is this and that doesn't matter so much.

This effect could be species specific thing or BS conversion efficiency problem. If the latter, methylation levels from different contexts might be correlated when you are looking at tiles.

I don't think this is a problem with methylKit.

Best,
Altuna

Many thanks for your help
Best regards
Alice

messages.subject: AssociationWithTSS genes
messages.body_plain:
hi All.

I am doing a methylkit analysis and i Have a question about my AssociationWith TSS file.  There are ~11,000 gene associations but I only found 321 regions that were deferentially methylated at 25%. Even with removing genes that were duplicated on the list, there are still over ~2000 unique genes. I don't understand how we have more gene associations than we do regions that were deferentially methylated. I am looking at 100bp windows. I was thinking that each region will have just one gene nearest to the TSS. Would you help me understand what s happening?

Thanks,

Roxy
